title: Replay tooling: operator API/command to replay an audit-event time window to a destination (with safeguards)
creator: Sean Gallagher
description:
Problem
Customers (and Support/SRE) need a safe way to re-deliver audit events when a destination experiences an outage/misconfiguration (e.g., Splunk 5xx / auth rotation / temporary egress issue). For beta we are explicitly at-least-once; replays will create duplicates unless customer dedupes using the documented event_id/dedupe key. We need a first-class operator tool that:
- can replay a bounded time window for a single destination
- is auditable and difficult to use accidentally
- works in Hosted/Dedicated and has a reasonable story in Private deployments

Context / references
- Delivery semantics ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0217-audit-export-delivery-semantics.json
- Filtering + delivery guarantees spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/audit-export-filtering-and-delivery-guarantees.json
- Runbook (lag/drain/replay): sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/audit-export-backlog-drain-replay.json

Goals (MVP for beta)
1) Provide an authenticated operator-only API to request a replay for destination D over [start_ts, end_ts).
2) Enforce strong safeguards (time window limits, confirmation workflow, audit logging, rate limiting, and destination state checks).
3) Provide operator visibility: status/progress of replay, expected duplicate behavior, and clear error messages.
4) Ensure replay does not compromise primary API latency (replay work should be queued/low-priority and backpressure-aware).

Non-goals (beta)
- Customer self-serve replay in Console (we can expose later behind additional permissions).
- Exactly-once guarantees.
- Large historical backfills (months) for all tenants.

Proposed design
A) Control plane: create a ReplayRequest object
- New internal endpoint (control plane):
  - POST /internal/audit-export/destinations/{destination_id}/replay
  - Request fields: start_time, end_time, dry_run (optional), reason (required), requested_by (derived), confirm_token (optional)
  - Response fields: replay_id, status, limits_applied, estimated_event_count (best-effort), warnings (duplicates, sink semantics)
- ReplayRequest stored in audit-export control-plane DB with state machine:
  - requested -> pending_confirmation -> queued -> running -> completed | failed | canceled
- Write an audit log event for every state transition (esp. requested/confirmed/canceled/completed) with destination_id, tenant/workspace, window, actor.

B) Safeguards / constraints
- Authorization:
  - Operator-only (SRE + Security Eng) via existing internal auth; no customer tokens.
  - Explicit permission gate: audit_export:replay (align with ENG-13933 RBAC hardening).
- Two-step confirmation (to prevent fat-finger):
  - Step 1 creates ReplayRequest in pending_confirmation and returns confirm_token + summary.
  - Step 2: POST .../replay/{replay_id}/confirm with confirm_token.
  - Optional bypass for on-call breakglass role (still audited) — confirm with Security Eng.
- Hard limits:
  - Max window duration: 60 minutes (configurable per deployment); reject larger windows.
  - Max replays per destination: 1 active (running/queued) at a time.
  - Max replay requests per tenant per hour: rate limit to prevent storms.
- Destination state checks:
  - Only allow replay when destination is Enabled or Degraded (not Paused/Deleted).
  - Require destination config unchanged since the window start OR surface a warning requiring explicit override flag (to avoid replaying to a newly re-pointed endpoint).
- Backpressure:
  - Replay jobs enqueue work onto the same durable queue but with a low-priority lane (or separate queue) to avoid starving real-time delivery.
  - If backlog_estimate exceeds threshold, require a manual override and emit warning.

C) Data plane: how replay is executed
- The replay worker queries the audit log store (or event archive) by tenant + time range, applying:
  - The destination’s filter rules as of “now” (beta) unless we can cheaply snapshot filter version; if filters changed, warn in summary.
- For each event in range, deliver using the existing sink connector path.
- Checkpointing / idempotency:
  - Replay does not mutate the “live” checkpoint used by normal streaming export.
  - Replay uses replay_id-scoped checkpoints so it can resume if worker crashes.
  - Emit replay metrics separately (replay_success_count, replay_failure_count, replay_latency) and tag with destination_type.

D) Operator UX
- Primary interface is API + a minimal CLI wrapper used by SRE/Support.
- Follow-up (separate ticket if needed): integrate with incident-bot command for status, not for triggering (keep trigger gated).

Acceptance criteria
- A replay request can be created for a destination and confirmed, resulting in re-delivery of events in the specified window.
- Safeguards enforced:
  - window <= max; destination must exist and be in allowed states
  - two-step confirmation required
  - rate limits prevent repeated triggers
  - audit log entries generated for request/confirm/cancel/complete with actor + reason
- Replay status is observable:
  - control plane exposes replay state + counters (processed/succeeded/failed) and last_error
  - metrics emitted and visible in dashboards (can be stubbed for beta if dashboard work is tracked elsewhere)
- Replay does not modify the primary streaming checkpoint.
- Works in Hosted and Dedicated; in Private, endpoint is available behind internal auth (document any extra steps for cluster operators).

Implementation plan (high-level)
1) Control-plane model + endpoints
- Add ReplayRequest table/model (replay_id, destination_id, tenant_id, start/end, reason, requested_by, confirmed_by, status, counters, created/updated).
- Implement POST request + confirm endpoints.
- Implement cancel endpoint (POST /internal/.../replay/{replay_id}/cancel) for stuck jobs.

2) Worker execution
- Add replay job consumer.
- Implement scan/query for events in time range (paginated) and enqueue deliveries.
- Add replay-specific checkpoint store.

3) Safeguards
- Destination config hash/version capture at request time; compare at confirm time.
- Rate limit + single-active-replay lock.
- Two-step confirmation + explicit summary/warnings.

4) Observability
- Structured logs with replay_id.
- Metrics: replay_requested_total, replay_confirmed_total, replay_events_processed_total, replay_events_failed_total, replay_duration_seconds.

5) Testing
- Unit tests: window validation, state transitions, rate limit, config-change warning behavior.
- Integration tests: replay over mocked sink; crash/restart resumes from replay checkpoint.

Open questions
- Source of truth for historical events in Private: do we query the same audit event store or rely on a bounded retention buffer? If retention differs, we should return “not available” for older windows.
- Filter versioning: do we need “apply filters as-of time T” for beta? Likely not, but we must warn loudly when filters changed recently.
- Should replay be able to target S3 only (initially) for large backfills? Not in beta scope, but might be requested.

Risks
- Accidental replay to a newly reconfigured destination causing data exposure or confusion. Mitigated by config-hash check + confirmation + audit logging.
- Replay storms increasing connector throttling. Mitigated by rate limits + low-priority queue + single-active-replay rule.

Deliverables
- Internal operator API + minimal CLI wrapper
- ReplayRequest state machine + audit trails
- Worker support + replay metrics
- Runbook updates and clear operator guidance on duplicates/dedupe keys (link to existing doc; update wording if needed)
comments: 2025-02-13 — Sean Gallagher (SRE): We need this before enabling the first 3 design partners. Last incident we ended up manually poking the worker and it was too easy to make things worse. Please keep trigger as operator-only for beta; status can be exposed more widely.

2025-02-14 — Marcus Lin (Security Eng): Strong requirement: audit log the replay request/confirm/cancel/complete actions, including destination_id + tenant_id + time window + reason. Also add a config-version check so we don’t replay to a changed endpoint without explicit override.

2025-02-18 — Benji Okafor: Drafted API shape and state machine. Planning to store destination_config_hash at request time and validate at confirm. Will need a low-priority lane in the queue; coordinating with ENG-13923 owner.

2025-02-21 — Rafael Mendes (SRE): Add a hard cap of 60m windows for beta and a single-active replay lock per destination. Also need cancel endpoint for stuck replays so on-call can stop runaway retries.

2025-03-01 — Kevin Osei (Security Eng): Please ensure replay cannot be triggered by customer API keys even in Private. In Private, cluster operator auth is fine, but must be clearly documented and logged.

2025-03-04 — Benji Okafor: Implemented ReplayRequest model + request/confirm endpoints behind internal auth (WIP). Next: worker consumer + replay checkpoint store; then wire audit log events and rate limiting.
